scenes.script: What if a modern water engineer
woke up in ancient Rome?
Day 1: You wake beside the Forum.
Phone dead. Shoes wrong. Latin everywhere.
Then you smell the part the marble hides.
Day 2: The water official inspects an aqueduct.
He measures by rank, habit, and favors.
Illegal pipes hide under respectable stone.
The rich get fountains. The upper floors get thirst.
Day 3: You draw the system in wax.
Same water. Calibrated outlets. Public measurements.
A builder asks who gave you authority.
You say water theft hides inside bad measurements.
The workers understand before the officials do.
By sunset, the quiet pipes are being checked.
Day 4: The contractors hear your name.
Guards arrive before breakfast.
They leave the diagram untouched.
They call you unauthorized.
Day 5: A Greek surveyor sits beside you.
He says Rome loves numbers until numbers cost money.
You tell him the gauges stay public.
He smiles like he has waited years.
Day 6: A magistrate demands the tablets.
He says the old system keeps order.
The workers keep copying your numbers.
Day 7: They come for you at dawn.
The street is already full.
Rome needs no future machine. It needs honest measurements.
